prompt: Why does this book use a zone, not a single line, for support and resistance?

options.text: Turns happened across a band of prices, not at one exact price
A line cannot be drawn on a chart
A zone makes the stop smaller

explanations.b: A zone does not guarantee anything. It describes where past turns clustered.
explanations.c: A line can be drawn. A line hides the spread of the past turns.
explanations.d: A zone does not change the stop size by itself. The stop goes beyond the zone.

options.text: A broken support can later act as resistance, and a broken resistance can later act as support
The price moves in the opposite direction to the volume
A stop is moved to the other side of the trade

explanations.b: A broken support does not always keep its job. Its job can change.
explanations.c: Volume and price direction are separate measures. Role reversal is about a broken level.
explanations.d: Moving a stop to the other side is not role reversal. Role reversal describes a broken level.

prompt: Hypothetical. A level has held three times. A trader says: 'It held three times, so it will hold a fourth time.' What is the best reply?

options.text: Agreed. Three holds make a fourth hold likely.
The three holds describe the past. They do not give a chance of a fourth hold. Test the level with a rule before you rely on it.
Only true if the level is a round number.
The level will fail, because it has held too often.

explanations.a: Three past holds do not make a fourth hold likely. Touch count is not a probability.
explanations.c: Round numbers do not change this. Touch count still describes the past only.
explanations.d: Past holds do not predict failure either. Both claims go beyond the evidence.

prompt: Spot the mistake: 'Support is a band of past buying. I will place my stop exactly on the line at Rs 249, because that is where buyers stepped in.' Which part is wrong?

options.text: Support is a band of past buying
I will place my stop exactly on the line at Rs 249
Because that is where buyers stepped in

explanations.a: This part is correct. Support is a band of past buying, not a single line.
explanations.c: This describes a past event. It is a reason for the zone, not a mistake. The error is the stop placement.
explanations.d: There is a mistake. Stops go beyond the zone, because normal noise touches its edges.

prompt: Hypothetical. A zone runs from Rs 380 to Rs 384. Entry Rs 384, stop Rs 377, capital Rs 40,000, risk 1 percent, concentration cap 25 percent. What are the final shares?
solution: Risk budget = Rs 400. Risk per share = 384 minus 377 = Rs 7. Raw shares = floor(400 / 7) = 57. Cash cap = floor(40,000 / 384) = 104. Concentration cap = floor(10,000 / 384) = 26. Final shares = minimum of 57, 104 and 26 = 26.

prompt: Hypothetical. In the worked example, the final shares are 49 with a risk per share of Rs 5. What is the planned loss at the stop, in rupees?
solution: Planned loss = shares x risk per share = 49 x 5 = 245. Check: 50 x 5 = 250, and 250 minus 5 = 245. The result is inside the Rs 500 risk budget.
